methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a local native represent grassroots peer-learning infrastructure that could distribute capability beyond metro concentration, signaling community-driven depth if sustained beyond initial outreach.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership concentrates AI education infrastructure in Richmond's institutional core, deepening metro hub capability but not yet demonstrating rural distribution mechanisms.

signals.title: UMW Launches Virginia’s First Master’s Degree in AI in Business - University of Mary Washington
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's first AI-in-Business master's degree creates credentialed expertise but concentration at UMW (Fredericksburg corridor) reinforces metro knowledge accumulation rather than distributed workforce transformation.

signals.title: More than 30,000 customers await broadband connections as provider struggles to complete work
signals.signal_reading: 30,000 customers awaiting broadband as provider struggles reveals infrastructure failure that blocks both shallow platform access and deep capability development in rural regions, entrenching the gap.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Direct analysis of how data center concentration in NoVA exacerbates urban-rural divide signals infrastructure investment patterns that deepen geographic inequality in AI economy participation.
